newsitem.title: USA: Leading indicators rise 0.1 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: Leading indicators rise 0.1 percent in November.

text.p: A key guage of economic activity inched higher in November, the Conference Board said on Monday, suggesting the expansion will continue in the months ahead.
The Index of Leading Indicators, which is designed to forecast economic trends six to nine months down the road, rose 0.1 percent in the month after holding steady in October.
The board had said previously that the October index rose 0.1 percent. The November rise was identical to Wall Street estimates.
Five of the 10 indicators rose, four declined and one was unchanged. The largest increases were in stock prices, money supply, consumer expectations and building permits.
The declines included interest rate spread and manufacturers' new orders of non-defence capital goods and consumer goods and materials.
The report reflected changes made in calculating the index to refine its ability to forecast turning points in the economy. Two of its components were dropped and a new one was added.
The board also calculated the index using the chain weighted method now used by the Commerce Department.
The base year for all indexes was also changed to 1992 from 1987.
